patients.summary: Young sales representative with plaque psoriasis on topicals and seasonal allergic rhinitis who joined the practice in 2024. Two weeks after his December 2025 physical he developed chlamydial urethritis treated at urology, then reactive arthritis (HLA-B27 positive) managed by rheumatology through remission in July 2026; the practice has these only as letters.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller lives in Amherst and wants a PCP closer to home; his previous office is a long drive. Has a skin condition (psoriasis), uses creams and a shampoo, no other meds he can think of. Employer PPO card info taken. Scheduled new pt physical 1/30 at 8:20, asked him to come fasting. Records release form emailed to eli.hale@example.test.

medications.sig: Apply thin layer to affected plaques twice daily as needed
Lather into scalp, leave 5 minutes, rinse; use twice weekly

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M establishing care, wants a doctor in town. Sales rep, lots of driving between client sites. Prior PCP records requested.

PMH:
- Plaque psoriasis since about age 15. Elbows, knees, some scalp scaling. Uses clobetasol 0.05% ointment twice a day on active plaques when they flare, and ketoconazole 2% shampoo twice a week for the scalp. Says this keeps it to a few coin-sized spots. Never on pills or injections for it.
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis, worst April-May and again September. Sneezing, itchy eyes, gets by without meds.
PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: clobetasol oint prn, ketoconazole shampoo 2x/wk.
Allergies: none to medications.
FHx: father has plaque psoriasis. Paternal uncle has ankylosing spondylitis. Mother on thyroid replacement for hypothyroidism.
Social: single, rents an apartment in town. Never smoked. 3-4 drinks a week, social. No drug use. Sexually active; offered condoms/STI counseling, accepted HIV and hep C screening today.

ROS: negative except a little dandruff-type flaking. No joint pain or morning stiffness, no eye problems, no GU complaints.

Exam: well-appearing young man. Vitals in flowsheet, BP normal. HEENT: TMs clear, nasal mucosa slightly pale, oropharynx normal. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: two well-demarcated scaly plaques, right elbow ~2 cm and left knee ~3 cm; fine scale along the posterior hairline. Nails without pitting. Joints: full range, no swelling or tenderness. Neuro grossly normal. Mood bright.

A/P:
1. Plaque psoriasis, limited, controlled on topicals. Continue both; reviewed not using clobetasol on face/groin and taking breaks once plaques flatten.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, mild, no treatment wanted.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, HIV, HCV today. PHQ-2 0. Tdap status pending old records. Flu shot declined today, will get it in the fall.
Follow up in a year or with any flare.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Eli, all of your bloodwork from yesterday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were both negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Records from former primary care office
documents.author: medical records
documents.body:
Received by fax, 22 pages, covering 2016-2023 from the patient's prior primary care office.

Summary of contents: well visits most years with normal exams. Psoriasis first noted on the elbows in 2016, treated with topical steroid; clobetasol ointment from 2019 onward, ketoconazole shampoo added in 2021 for scalp scale. Seasonal allergy symptoms noted in spring visits, no prescription. Oral surgery note 2019 for third molar extraction, uncomplicated. Immunizations: childhood series complete per school record, Tdap 08/07/2019. No drug allergies listed.

Abstracted to chart; reviewed by PCP.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request: clobetasol 0.05% ointment 60 g. Last filled by his former doctor. Seen 1/30, on med list, psoriasis controlled. Sent 60 g with 2 refills per PCP standing order.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after work for vaccines. Feels well, no fever. Screening questions negative. Flu vaccine L deltoid, COVID 2024-25 R deltoid. Lot numbers in immunization record. Waited 15 min without issue.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for his yearly skin check-in. Winter usually worse for him. Using clobetasol a few nights a week on the elbows, shampoo twice weekly. Scalp much better than last year. Denies joint pain, back stiffness, eye redness. Busy quarter at work, otherwise fine.

O: Vitals reviewed. Skin: small scaly plaque R elbow about 1.5 cm, faint pink patch L knee with minimal scale, scalp clear. No nail changes. No synovitis of hands, knees or ankles.

A/P: Plaque psoriasis, limited and stable on topicals. Continue current regimen, refills sent as needed. Discussed that if it spreads or joints start hurting, there are good systemic options and dermatology can see him. Physical due at the end of the year.

documents.title: Allergy season
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey doc, pollen is killing me this week, sneezing nonstop in the car between appointments. Same as every May. Anything you recommend besides waiting it out? Not trying to come in for it.

documents.title: RE: Allergy season
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, the tree pollen has been rough this year. Things that help without a visit: saline rinse of the nose once or twice a day, keep the car on recirculate with windows up, and shower before bed to get the pollen off your hair. If it is keeping you up at night or not easing by June, send me a note and we can talk about options.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: E-refill request ketoconazole 2% shampoo 120 mL, first time from our office. Routed to PCP, approved with 3 refills.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Early slot before his drive to a client. Well today. 2025-26 flu vaccine and 2025-26 COVID vaccine given, one each arm. Tolerated, left after observation. Reminded him his physical is due.

documents.title: Reschedule
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt has a sales conference out of state this week, can't make the 11/18 physical. Moved to Fri 12/26 at 9:40, he is off that week. Fasting labs same morning.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 y/o man for annual exam, rescheduled from November. Quiet week at work so he finally had time.

Interval: no illnesses, ER visits or new meds this year. Psoriasis stable, mostly elbows, uses clobetasol here and there and the shampoo twice weekly. Spring allergies were bad in May, saline helped some. No joint pain or stiffness, no eye issues, no urinary symptoms.
Meds: clobetasol 0.05% oint prn, ketoconazole 2% shampoo twice weekly. NKDA.
Social: same job, a lot of time on the road. Never smoker. Alcohol about 3-4 drinks/week. Exercises at a gym 2x/week.
FHx unchanged (father psoriasis, uncle AS, mother hypothyroid).

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, normal. Weight about the same as last year. Eyes and ENT normal. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Skin: one small plaque R elbow, otherwise clear; scalp clear. MSK: spine with normal motion, no peripheral joint swelling. Neuro intact.

Assessment/plan:
- Well adult exam. CBC, CMP, lipid panel today. Vaccines current (flu and COVID in October; Tdap 2019).
- Plaque psoriasis, quiet. No change.
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis, symptomatic only in spring.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Eli, your labs from Friday all look good. Cholesterol, blood counts, kidney and liver function are normal. See you next year. Happy new year.

documents.title: Urology office visit with addendum
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Date of service: 01/09/2026. Addendum: 01/12/2026. Copy to primary care.

Reason for visit: dysuria and urethral discharge.

Mr. Hale is a 25-year-old man who self-scheduled with three days of burning on urination and a thin, clear discharge from the penis. About two weeks before the symptoms began he had condomless sex with a new partner. He has not traveled, knows of no one ill around him, and has never had anything like this before. No fever, flank pain, testicular pain or rash.

History: plaque psoriasis on topical therapy; seasonal allergies. Third molars removed at 18.
Medications: clobetasol 0.05% ointment as needed to plaques; ketoconazole 2% shampoo twice weekly.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father with psoriasis; paternal uncle with ankylosing spondylitis; mother with hypothyroidism.
Social: sales representative, never smoker, 3-4 drinks weekly.

Exam: afebrile, vital signs normal. Genitourinary: clear mucoid urethral discharge at the meatus. No ulcers, vesicles or warts, no erythema. Testes descended, nontender, no masses; epididymides normal. No inguinal adenopathy.

Data: office urinalysis without white cells or bacteria; nitrite and leukocyte esterase negative. Urethral specimen sent for chlamydia and gonorrhea nucleic acid amplification.

Impression: urethritis, likely sexually acquired; await NAAT.

ADDENDUM 01/12/2026: Chlamydia trachomatis NAAT detected. Neisseria gonorrhoeae NAAT not detected. Diagnosis: chlamydial urethritis. Patient reached by phone and informed. Doxycycline 100 mg by mouth twice daily for 7 days sent to his pharmacy. Counseled to avoid sex for 7 days after finishing treatment and until partners are treated; he will notify his recent partner, who should be tested and treated. Retest in about 3 months recommended. Follow up with us as needed.

documents.title: Urology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I saw a urologist last week for a urinary thing, turned out to be chlamydia. They put me on doxycycline and I'm on day 3, already better. Embarrassing but figured you should have it in my file.

documents.title: RE: Urology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, Eli, and nothing to be embarrassed about. We got their letter. Finish all 7 days of the doxycycline, take it with a full glass of water and stay upright for a bit afterward, and go easy on sun exposure while you're on it. Retesting in about 3 months is a good idea. Reach out if anything new comes up.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Consultation date: 02/12/2026. Results completed 02/17/2026.

Patient: 25-year-old male, self-referred via urgent scheduling line; copy to PCP.

CC: joint swelling, eye redness, urinary pain.

HPI: Chlamydia urethritis diagnosed by urology in early January and treated with a week of doxycycline, roughly one month ago. For the last two weeks the dysuria has returned, his right eye has been red and sore, and over the past several days the left knee and right ankle became suddenly painful and swollen, making it hard to walk the trade-show floor. No injury to either joint. Background plaque psoriasis on topicals.

Meds: clobetasol ointment prn, ketoconazole shampoo. NKDA.
Family: father psoriasis; paternal uncle ankylosing spondylitis; mother hypothyroidism.
Social: sales rep. Never smoker; drinks socially. Reports several sexual partners recently with inconsistent condom use.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. R eye: conjunctiva injected, no discharge visible at the lids. Purulent urethral discharge noted. L knee: effusion, warm, painful at end range. R ankle: swollen and warm over the tibiotalar joint. Other joints without synovitis. Spine nontender. Skin: no psoriatic plaques at present, no lesions of palms, soles or glans. Nails normal.

Labs (02/12): ESR 50 mm/hr (ref 0-22). CRP 25 mg/L (ref <5.0). UA with pyuria. Urethral swab: gonorrhea NAAT not detected. Repeat chlamydia NAAT not detected. HLA-B27 positive.

Assessment: reactive arthritis following chlamydial urethritis: asymmetric lower-limb oligoarthritis with urethritis and eye inflammation, HLA-B27 positive, which together with the uncle's ankylosing spondylitis fits the B27-associated spectrum. Prior infection adequately treated; repeat chlamydia test negative.

Plan:
1. Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food. Reviewed stomach and kidney cautions; avoid other NSAIDs.
2. Urgent ophthalmology this week to exclude anterior uveitis; appointment made for 02/16.
3. Rest the ankle, ice; activity as tolerated.
4. Return in about 8 weeks with ESR, CRP, CBC, CMP. Sooner for worsening eye pain or vision change.
5. Safer-sex counseling given.

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside eye clinic. Exam date 02/16/2026. Referred by rheumatology; cc primary care.

Reason: red, sore right eye in a patient with newly diagnosed reactive arthritis.

History: right eye red and achy for about two weeks, no blur. No contact lenses. No eye history. Meds include naproxen, topical clobetasol, ketoconazole shampoo. NKDA.

Exam: VA 20/20 OD and OS uncorrected. Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. IOP 15 OD, 14 OS. External/lids normal. Conjunctiva: diffuse injection OD, white OS. Cornea clear OU, no staining. Anterior chamber deep and quiet OU, no cells or flare. Lens clear. Dilated fundus: healthy optic nerves, normal macula, vessels and periphery OU.

Impression: conjunctivitis of the right eye related to reactive arthritis. No uveitis.

Plan: preservative-free artificial tears as needed. He knows to return promptly for pain, light sensitivity or blurred vision, since uveitis can occur with HLA-B27. Routine follow-up as needed.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update since the chlamydia thing turned into more. Rheumatology says it's reactive arthritis and I'm on naproxen. Eye doctor said the eye is fine, no uveitis. Knee is better already, ankle still puffy. Do I need to do anything with you guys?

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Eli, thanks for the update. Both letters are in your chart and the doctor has seen them. Rheumatology is running this for now, so keep their follow-up. Take the naproxen with food and let them know if you get heartburn or dark stools. Nothing else needed from us right now; we'll catch up at your next visit.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology follow-up, seen 04/16/2026. Copy to PCP.

Interval: eye cleared within a couple of weeks; no urinary symptoms since February. Knee pain gone. Right ankle still slightly swollen by evening after long days standing. Taking naproxen twice daily with meals, no stomach upset or dark stools.

Exam: BP and pulse normal. Left knee without effusion, full motion. Right ankle with mild residual soft tissue swelling, minimal warmth, near-full motion. No new joints. Eyes white. No skin lesions.

Labs 04/16: ESR 26 mm/hr. CRP 7.8 mg/L. CBC and CMP within normal limits, creatinine normal.

Assessment: reactive arthritis, improving on NSAID.
Plan: continue naproxen 500 mg twice daily for now; recheck in about 3 months with ESR and CRP. Call if the ankle flares or the eye becomes painful.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology return visit 07/09/2026; letter to PCP.

Doing well. No joint pain or swelling for about six weeks, back to full workdays on his feet and to the gym. No eye or urinary symptoms. Has been taking naproxen once a day or skipping it lately.

Exam: vitals normal. All peripheral joints without swelling, warmth or tenderness, full range including the right ankle and left knee. Eyes white. Skin without active plaques.

Labs 07/09: ESR 11 mm/hr, CRP 2.1 mg/L.

Assessment: reactive arthritis in remission.
Plan: stop naproxen. No scheduled follow-up; he will call us if joint swelling, heel or low back pain, or eye symptoms return, given HLA-B27 positivity. Primary care to continue routine care.

documents.title: Appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Rheum discharged me, joints are all good now. Can I set up a visit with Dr. to go over everything from this year? Afternoons after 3 work best, sometime in September.

documents.title: RE: Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Glad you're feeling better! You're booked Thursday 9/10 at 3:30. Let us know if that needs to change.
